speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are a young patient presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To understand the underlying cause, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if the lesions are itchy, painful, or draining fluid?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Septic Arthritis (Left Wrist) secondary to Bartonella henselae infection.

The history of a self-resolving knee pain followed by current wrist pain, fever, and recent camping exposure strongly suggests disseminated cat scratch disease causing septic arthritis. I need to confirm the nature of the skin lesions and your cat exposure history to solidify this.
